title: The Ears Did the Work
concept: An AI picker, EQTransformer, retrained by G. Barcheck (Cornell) and N. A. Ruppert (USGS) on a hand-checked catalog from the 2018 to 2019 Alaska Amphibious Community Seismic Experiment (75 seafloor and 30 land seismometers), found roughly three times as many earthquakes along the Alaska Peninsula than the analyst-checked catalog, per the authors' abstract. No training strategy was substantially better, local data was what improved it, and the biggest gains were far offshore and in the outer rise. The film credits the ears and the pencils, shows the check that passed (same map) and the limit (one temporary experiment, more heard not more shaking), and ends asking whether Alaska keeps putting ears on the seafloor. Bunk, a mint-domed seafloor seismometer, is the hero and the catalog Sheet is the throughline.

divergence_note: The last films were a midnight indigo cab with sodium amber and teal (11-02), a storm slate slope with sulphur (11-01), a cream chart desk with cobalt and brass (10-31), an aubergine dusk depot (10-29) and a green-black sonar abyss (10-28). This film is oxblood and wine with mint, gold and chalk, played on a stage over a seafloor cutaway. Its hero is a mint-domed seafloor seismometer, its stage opens front-on with a trapdoor cut rather than a floor cutaway and it closes on an aerial grid, it has no cab, no slope, no desk, no depot and no green-black sonar, and its signature object is a catalog Sheet whose dots go chalk, gold and outline.

treatment.title: The Robot Takes a Bow
treatment.summary: Comedian's stage and bow, with the Dramatist's limit scene, the Explainer's waterline and the Enthusiast's Sheet.

angle.thesis: The credit belongs to the data, not the algorithm: no training trick won, and Alaska's own human-checked earthquake picks, recorded by 75 seafloor and 30 land seismometers, taught an existing AI picker to find roughly three times as many quakes, most of the gain far offshore.
supporting_facts: c11 no training strategy was substantially better
c12 local waveform data set improved performance
c14 roughly 3x more earthquakes than the analyst-checked catalog (this 2018-2019 catalog only)
c16 biggest gains far offshore and outer rise
angle.falsifiability: False if a training trick clearly beat the others, if extra quakes scattered off known structure, or if gains were not concentrated offshore. Abstract says the opposite on all three. False-positive rate unknown (paper body unreachable).
angle.counterpoint: Temporary 2018-2019 experiment, judged from an abstract with no absolute counts. Roughly 3x says nothing about whether seismicity rose or what a permanent network hears today. The expensive part (a dense seafloor array and hand-checked labels) came first. Open question: does Alaska keep putting sensors on the seafloor to feed the recipe?
angle.second_movement: The headline reads AI breakthrough, the paper's own finding is data decided it. Credit moves to the people who deployed instruments and checked picks by hand.

runner_ups.dramatist: what does the AI hear once the seafloor stations are pulled up (kept as the Act 3 TEST and the button question)
runner_ups.explainer: falling tide image (kept as the physical comparison for completeness)

guardrails: roughly, per the authors, no absolute counts
not an Alaska Earthquake Center product
no forecast, no causal link to 1938 or 2021 quakes, no 'same segment' without hedge
